why: Every part is specified (the audience groups, tokens, rule classification, the two lines, the SQL, the card and its strings) and no design choice is left. The weak spot is commit 1: a long measuring script that becomes a failing CI step, built on step 1.8's reach() whose signature the brief assumes, and its only check of correctness is that the first run lands in the review's ranges. A model that tunes the classification to fit those ranges would pass every check with a wrong figure. Commits 2 and 3 are a read-only, on-demand platform-admin card and docs, with unit and int tests, touching no money or permissions.
harm_if_wrong: A miscounting audiences script would hold or fail CI on wrong numbers and steer step 2.11's split, and a wrong SQL filter would misstate owners' style text on a platform-only screen.
make_it_cheaper: Give reach()'s exact signature and return type from step 1.8's file, plus a planted fixture (a tiny .next/static sheet and three source files) that the unit test runs end to end with known byte counts; commit 1 would then be cheap.
brief_problems: pnpm-lock.yaml holds two postcss versions (8.5.23 and 8.5.28); 'the version the lockfile already has for @tailwindcss/postcss' needs the exact one named.

The SQL counts pages with `p.published is not null` and sums header/footer CSS without a publish filter, while src/server/site-layouts.ts treats a layout as live only when `p.published_at is not null`; the reading may count drafts that were once published.
scripts/lib/import-walk.mjs (step 1.8) and the budgets rule file (step 1.1) do not exist yet; reach(srcDir, entry, { dynamic: true }) is assumed, not shown.
